seoTitle: How to Add Bulk Users in Google Workspace (2026)
metaDescription: Learn how Google Workspace admins can add many users at once using CSV import in the Admin Console, from file prep to verifying the new accounts.
intro: Manually creating accounts one by one doesn't scale when you're onboarding a whole team or department. This guide shows Workspace admins how to use the Admin Console's bulk import tool to add multiple users at once with a CSV file.

steps.heading: Access the Admin Console
steps.body: Sign in with a super admin account and navigate to the Users section, where the bulk upload option lives.

steps.heading: Prepare your CSV file
steps.body: Download Google's CSV template and fill in each new user's required details — name, username, and password — following the exact column format.

steps.heading: Import the CSV file
steps.body: Upload the completed file through the bulk update users tool; Google Workspace processes it and creates the accounts in batch.

steps.heading: Verify the added users
steps.body: Once the import finishes, check the Users list to confirm every account was created correctly and fix any rows that failed to import.

faq.question: Is there a limit to how many users I can add in one CSV upload?
faq.answer: Google Workspace supports bulk uploads of hundreds of users per file, though very large organizations may need to split imports into multiple batches.

faq.question: What happens if a row in my CSV has an error?
faq.answer: The Admin Console flags rows with formatting or data errors so you can fix and re-upload just those entries without redoing the whole file.

faq.question: Do bulk-added users need to change their password on first login?
faq.answer: You can require a password reset on first sign-in as part of the CSV import, which is standard practice for security.

faq.question: Can I use bulk import to update existing users instead of just adding new ones?
faq.answer: Yes, the same bulk upload tool supports updating certain fields for existing accounts, not just creating new ones.
